nodes.label: Explicit Failure Semantics
nodes.rationale: Missing configuration, capability, data, or design decisions must surface as errors instead of being hidden by implicit fallbacks, limits, assumptions, or defaults.

nodes.label: Runtime Service Boundary
nodes.rationale: Heavy training, prediction, embedding, and image dependencies stay outside HTTP request execution and do not import API internals.

nodes.label: Resource Automation
nodes.rationale: Automations are target-bound and recipe-constrained so ordinary users configure business run modes without constructing arbitrary workflows.

nodes.label: Dataset Revision
nodes.rationale: Lightweight immutable revisions preserve audit and provenance without copying every sample, annotation, or image or claiming full reproducibility.

nodes.label: Collection Snapshot
nodes.rationale: Snapshots publish observed member revisions and mappings while treating complete merged data as rebuildable cache rather than archival truth.

nodes.label: Bulk Table-First Data Path
nodes.rationale: Large data paths use LazyFrame, DataFrame, Arrow tables, scans, joins, batches, and streaming writers to avoid unbounded Python row-object processing.

nodes.label: Registry and Descriptor Extension
nodes.rationale: Extension points are registered through module-owned registries and descriptors to prevent hardcoded central switch statements.

nodes.label: Explicit Organization Context
nodes.rationale: Organization isolation must not depend on an implicit global default.

nodes.label: Data Strategy Ownership
nodes.rationale: Algorithms own selection, construction, loading, batching, and output semantics instead of a central materializer or universal runtime I/O model.

nodes.label: Port-App-Domain Dependency Direction
nodes.rationale: Layer direction and Protocol-typed services isolate pure business rules from HTTP, persistence, and runtime adapters.

nodes.label: Interface-Only Cross-Module Dependencies
nodes.rationale: Explicit narrow Protocols keep module internals private and prevent refactors from preserving concrete coupling under new names.

nodes.label: Composition Migration Order
nodes.rationale: Interface-based composition precedes storage and runtime extraction because those boundaries depend on removing concrete cross-module coupling.

nodes.label: Table-First Prediction Writeback
nodes.rationale: Prediction results move as Parquet or Arrow batches and manifests rather than one request per prediction row.

nodes.label: Explicit Missing-Data Semantics
nodes.rationale: Every image-bearing path must choose fail or skip explicitly and represent partial failures with counters and error data.

nodes.label: Sparse Mode Intent
nodes.rationale: Large datasets prioritize shard-native ingest, batch prediction, and sparse correction rather than recreating full SampleORM and Label Studio parity.

nodes.label: Storage Mode Orthogonality
nodes.rationale: Physical storage behavior is selected explicitly and is never inferred from semantic dataset type.

nodes.label: Algorithm-Owned Runtime Context
nodes.rationale: Runtime contexts carry dispatch identity and options but do not impose universal algorithm input, output, materialization, or batching semantics.

nodes.label: Import-Safe Registration
nodes.rationale: Registration metadata remains importable by the API without loading Torch, CUDA, model weights, or performing I/O.

nodes.label: DuckDB Query Security
nodes.rationale: AST validation and connection hardening jointly restrict queries to authorized read-only views and block DDL, DML, extensions, files, and networks.

nodes.label: Local Selection Constraints
nodes.rationale: Selection remains compact frontend state and query constraints so large result sets are not materialized as IDs or persisted as server columns.

nodes.label: Prefect Compensation
nodes.rationale: Best-effort compensation handles partial failure because Prefect and the product database do not share a transaction.

nodes.label: Collection Automation Non-Goals
nodes.rationale: The plan excludes content hashing, cross-collection dataset reuse, historical backfill, automatic promotion, arbitrary workflows, partitions, raw cron editing, and automatic snapshot refresh.
